title: Griddhakuta Hill (Vulture’s Peak), Rajgir - The Sacred Meditation Site of Lord Buddha
content:
Griddhakuta Hill (Vulture’s Peak), Rajgir

Griddhakuta Hill, also known as Vulture’s Peak, is one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage sites in Rajgir, Bihar. Perched amidst the picturesque Rajgir hills, this tranquil spot holds immense historical and spiritual significance as it was a favored meditation and preaching site of Lord Buddha. The hill gets its name from its shape, which resembles a vulture sitting with folded wings.

Historical Significance

Griddhakuta Hill is where Lord Buddha delivered several important sermons, including many teachings from the Lotus Sutra. It was also here that King Bimbisara of Magadha frequently visited Buddha to listen to his discourses. The site marks the early spread of Buddhism and the foundation of the First Buddhist Council, held soon after Buddha’s Mahaparinirvana.

The hill is surrounded by ancient rock formations, Buddhist stupas, and meditation caves, where monks and followers continue to meditate even today.

Spiritual Experience

Visiting Griddhakuta Hill offers a sense of deep peace and connection to the teachings of the Buddha. Pilgrims often walk the stone-paved path or take the Rajgir ropeway that leads up to the Vishwa Shanti Stupa, which lies close by. The summit provides a mesmerizing view of the Rajgir valley, filled with greenery and sacred monasteries.

At sunrise and sunset, the golden light falling on the hills creates an atmosphere of divine serenity, making it a must-visit spot for spiritual seekers and nature lovers alike.

Visitor Information

  • Location: Rajgir, Nalanda District, Bihar
  • Timings: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free
  • How to Reach: By ropeway or by trekking up the stone steps from the base of the hill
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March
